rooms.name: A Corner in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
You are standing knee-high in filthy water deep within the sewer
system underneath the streets of Alaozar.  Everything from half-eaten
food to rotting corpses of dead animals float in this nasty water.  You
can continue to the south or east from this point.

rooms.name: In a Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This section of the sewers looks a bit older than the majority of the
tunnels you have seen.  Looking carefully at the walls you note that
there seem to be sealed tombs along them and deduce that this area used
to be a catacomb.  Dead rats and waste float past you in the water and
the stench is so bad here you nearly vmoit.  You can continue to the
east or west.

rooms.name: In the Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
The filthy water has grown more shallow here, thankfully, and you can
nearly see the brick floor as you walk through the filth.  Every so
often a gush of dirty water rushes out of little openings in the ceiling
and makes you scurry to get out of the way.  The northern wall here is
made of thick grey stone, instead of simple brick and mortar.  You can
go east or west.

rooms.name: In the Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
The water here is only an inch deep or so and it leaks through all
of the walls except the northern one which is made of re-enforced
grey stone and mortar.  On the southern wall you see what appear to
be well-sealed tombs and surmise that this area of the sewers may
have once been used as a catacomb.  You may proceed to the west or
east.

rooms.name: An Intersection in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
You have reached a kind of junction of sewer pipes.  One very small
pipe at ground level leads to the south and seems to connect this
pipe with another.  This pipe continues both east and west.

rooms.name: A Dry Room
rooms.desc:
Amazing, the ground here is totally dry and the filthy waters of the
sewer no longer surround and eat at your feet.  While the stench here
is not so bad as to the west, it is still pretty smelly.  This place
seems to be a dead-end room of some kind.  You do not know who would
ever build a room under a city in a maze of sewers, though!  Someone
has even bothered to hang a large, mud-caked area rug on the eastern
wall.  The only apparent exit is to the west.

rooms.name: In the Secret Passageway
rooms.desc:
Here, in a passageway with stone floors and a more raised dome than
most sewer pipes, the odor of decay and filth is not strong at all.
Through a mud-caked area rug to the west you can hear rushing water and
assume that the sewer system runs in that direction.  This passageway
leads off to the south into the darkness.  The only obvious exit
is to the south.

rooms.name: In a Large Sewer Pipe
rooms.desc:
You are standing in knee-high water inside a large sewer pipe under the
city of Alaozar.  Filthy gushes of water and waste rush down from small
openings in the ceiling of this pipe and cascade into the water in which
you stand.  The western wall, unlike the others, is made of huge grey
stones, iron spikes, and mortar.  A little brick passageway leads to the
north and seems to join this pipe with a smaller one.  This tunnel itself
continues to the east.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
From this point, a rather large sewer pipe leads both east and west while
yet another smaller pipe runs off to the south into the distance.  The
water here is pretty dirty; full of trash, dirt, and waste.  Needless to
say, the smell is very unpleasant, too.

rooms.name: In a Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are wading through waist-high water carefully trying to avoid the many
floating collections of filth which share your bath.  There seems to be a
current here -- it is pushing you to the west.  This pipe leads both to the
east and west.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
Here, a small pipe intersects with a larger one and you are offered the
opportunity to go west, east, or south.  A current in the water is
pushing the filth inexorably.  The large pipe in which you stand runs east
and west while another pipe with a smaller diameter runs off to the south
seemingly connecting this tunnel to another.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
The current here has really picked up;  the water around you is being
pushed steadily to the west.  You find a dry ledge running parallel to
the flow along the wall and are, thankfully, able to stand on it rather
than in the filth.  A little tunnel leads north from here, seemingly
connecting this tunnel to another.  The pipe in which you stand leads
to the west and east.

rooms.name: At a Corner in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
Thankfully you are able to scoot along a thin lip on the wall here rather
than wade through the cold, filthy water.  And it's a good thing too, because
there seems to be a strong current swiftly moving the trash and waste along.
This pipe bends sharply here, causing a small whirlpool.  You can
continue to the south or move with the current to the west.

rooms.name: In a Dry Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This tunnel is made of strong grey rock and you suspect you are moving
through or near the city walls.  You notice a thick layer of dust on
the ground and wonder how long it has been since anyone has come this
way.  There is also a faint draft coming from the south.  You can go
north or south.

rooms.name: At a Dead-End in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
You have come to a dead-end with the only exit being to the east, against
the current.  The water here swirls and turns as more rushes and you are
forced to cling to one of the moldy walls to keep your balance.  You also
notice that the western wall is not like the others here -- it is made of
huge grey stones instead of old bricks.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
You have reached a four-way intersection; here, a smaller pipe leads to
the north and south while one with a larger diameter runs both east and
west.  Most of the water flows in from the north and east and rushes off
to the south.  There is a little whirlpool here and you notice water is
both leaving and returning from the west...  You can proceed in any dir-
ection.

rooms.name: At a Turn in the Sewer Pipe
rooms.desc:
The pipe you are in bends here leading west and south.  The floor of the
tunnel is very uneven and seems to almost slope against the current which
flows in from the south and runs off to the west.  As the water moves, it
rushes over the uneven floor making rapids.  You can go west or south.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
This sewer pipe is full of fast-moving water which enters from the east
and flows off to the south.  You also hear what sounds like an angry
river from the south.  A smaller pipe leads north connecting this tunnel
to yet another.

rooms.name: In a Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are standing on a ledge just above the raging waters which rush
through this pipe from east to west.  A plaque is set in the wall
here right next to where you crouch.  You may continue either west
or east.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
This is a very large pipe which seems to lead north and south.  You are
lucky to be up on the lip of the tunnel because huge amounts of water
run in from the south.  More than half of the current rushes down a
large tunnel to the west.  Some of the flow also runs to the north.
You may go north, west or south.

rooms.name: In a Dry Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You must be either directly under the wall or right next to it because
the stones all around you look exactly like the ones used to make the
town walls.  You notice that there are some very old chairs here and
what look to be several empty weapon cases.  While this tunnel only leads
to the north, there is a slight draft coming from the eastern wall!

rooms.name: At a Bend in the Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
The pipe in which you stand turns sharply here; water comes in from the
east, swirls around in a little whirlpool, and flows out to the south.
You are standing on a small ledge apparently built for sewer workers to
avoid getting their feet wet.  South of here the tunnel seems to open
into a very large tunnel.

rooms.name: At a Bend in the Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This section of the pipe seems to have been engineered and built to
slow down the current.  Its floor is very uneven and the water is
forced to flow around or over many obsticles made of brick.  You
also note that the grade of the ground is not even -- the water is
forced to rush uphill to the west and it able to only because of
it's momentum.  You may continue to the west or north.

rooms.name: In a Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are at a turn in this sewer pipe -- water that roars in from the
east spins for a while in a little whirlpool and then tears away to 
the north.  You are on a small ledge made of bricks and attached to
one wall praying that it does not give way and send you plummeting
into the filthy waters just below.  You can go north or east.

rooms.name: Under the Grate
rooms.desc:
You are standing in a sewer tunnel on a little ledge as dirty water
rushes past below you.  Far, far above you see a grate and, looking
carefully, espy a ladder that you might use to reach it.  This
sewer tunnel leads both west and north.

rooms.name: In a Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
The tunnel turns here and the clean water flows in from the south and
rushes away to the east.  Through an opening in the south wall you see
the massive Chartuse River tunnel and hear the roar of the entire river
as it gushes under town.  You can go south or east.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
Here the sewer tunnel in which you stand is joined by another leading to 
the north.  Clean water flows in from the west and rushes off to the
north.  You can also go east.

rooms.name: At a Dead-End in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
You have reached a dead-end... the only exit is to the west.  The water
here is about waist-deep and swirls around you and more water rushes in
from the west.

rooms.name: Room #21328
rooms.desc: This description is yet unfinished...

rooms.name: Behind the Grate
rooms.desc:
Wow... the current that pushes against you from the east is almost
unbelievable!  Although this massive tunnel leads east, you cannot
defeat the current to move that direction.  A large grate blocks your
way to the west and through it you see the outside world.  All around
you the waters of the Chartuse River roar as rush past, pin you to the
grate, and flow off to the west.  There is a medium-sized tunnel to
the north from which a stream of filth-ridden water joins the rest
of the river; you could probibly fight the strong current to reach
it.

rooms.name: In the Chartuse River Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are being swept along by the Chartuse River as it gushes through a
massive tunnel deep below Alaozar!  It is all you can do to maintain a
grip on the wall and prevent yourself from being swept away by the strong
current.  As you begin to lose you grip, you notice a passageway to the
south which emits a steady flow of filty water into the river.  Even-
though there is no possible way for you to fight the river and move
along this tunnel to the east, you do suspect you could reach the
tunnel in the southern wall.  You can also move with the current to
the west.

rooms.name: In the Chartuse River Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This massive tunnel is half-filled by the entire Chartuse River!  The
current here is almost indescribable... tons of water rush past you as
you desperatly cling to the moldy wall to prevent yourself from being
swept away.  There is very little you can do in this tunnel -- the
current is far too strong to fight and you cannot move to the east.
The only thing to do, it would seem, is move with the current to the
west.

rooms.name: In the Chartuse River Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This huge tunnel houses the entire Chartuse River!  The current here is
unbelievable and it is all you can do just to cling to a wall to prevent
youself from being swept away by the flood.  While the tunnel leads both
east and west, there is no way to fight the flow of this river by moving
to the east.  It would seem that the only thing to do is move with the
current to the west.

rooms.name: In the Chartuse River Tunnel
rooms.desc:
The current here is so strong that you cannot fight it and move to the
east.  While you cling to the moldy wall here, about to lose your grip,
thinking your only option is to carefully move with the water to the
west, you notice a tunnel carved into the northern wall into which some
of the water branches.  Perhaps you could reach it and go north...?

rooms.name: In the Chartuse River Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This massive subterranean tunnel houses the entire Chartuse River!  The
current is unimaginable and you are clinging to the slimey wall just to
keep yourself from being swept away by the tons of water rushing past
you.  Unfortunately, the river is far too strong to move against to the
east.  As you glance around, you see a tunnel leading south into which
a steady stream of water flows.  If you could just reach it without
losing your grip...

rooms.name: Behind the Grate
rooms.desc:
Maybe coming here was a mistake... the river seems to pick up speed
as it is forced into this large tunnel and the current here is amazing.
It is all you can do to hold on to the moldy wall and avoid being swept
away by the water.  Although you can see out a grate in the eastern wall,
there is just no way to move against the current and reach it.  As you
study your situation you realize that the only thing to do is move with
the current to the west and hope for the best.

rooms.name: Room #21336
rooms.desc: This description is yet unfinished...

rooms.name: At a Bend in the Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are standing in a filthy sewer tunnel; the water here is full of
dirt, grime, waste, and gunk that has dripped down through drainage
vents in town and collected in these waters.  The current moves to the
east.  You may go east or south.

rooms.name: A Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
You are standing where one large pipe joins with another.  North of here,
through a little tunnel, you hear the roar of water.  A filthy flow of
waste water rushes in from the west and gushes through the passage to
the north.  A ledge on the eastern wall seems to lead off to some dryer
tunnels.  You may go north, west or east.

rooms.name: In a Dry Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This tunnel was probibly not constructed as part of the sewers but rather,
you suspect, is older than the sewers and was perhaps used once as a cat-
acomb.  The ground and walls are not made of brick like the sewer system
but are, instead, made of stone and clay.  Judging from the amount of
dust here, no one has been this way in a while.  To the west, over a small
ledge, you see the sewer system.  East of here, this tunnel joins more
like it.

rooms.name: In a Dry Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are in a tunnel which is older than the sewer system of Alaozar.  This
place seems to have once been used as a burial ground judging from the seal-
ed tombs in the clay and stone walls.  As you look around carefully, you
notice some carving on one of the walls here.  This dry tunnel leads to
the west and east.

rooms.name: In a Strange Chamber
rooms.desc:
This place seems to be a big burial vault -- or at least at one time it
must have been.  There are tombs sealed in the walls and writing here
and there.  Now it would seem someone is living here!  There is a big,
old sofa next to one of the tombs and a little wooden table sitting in
the center of the room.  Passages lead off to the west and south.

rooms.name: At a bend in the Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are standing at a bend in the sewer tunnel perched atop a little lip
on one of the walls and thankful that you do not have to wade in this
water.  Every now and again streams of filth and dirt gush from tiny
holes in the ceiling and are embraced by the water flowing beneath you.
Current comes in from the east and rushes off to the south.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
The noise of rushing water to the north is almost deafening and the amount
of water that gushes in from the tunnel leading north is amazing.  This
pipe leads off to the west and the water follows it.  Over a tall dam,
a passageway also leads to the east.  Of course, you can also try to
fight the water current and move to the north.

rooms.name: In a Dry Room
rooms.desc:
This seems to be a single dry room.  Some iron pipes run along the walls
and up through the stone ceiling.  Wow, do people in the city above really
have running water?  The only exit seems to be to the west over a big dam
and back into the waters and sewer.

rooms.name: In a Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are standing in a sewer tunnel and are forced to actually wade through
the filth as the lip of this tunnel designed to allow people to walk here
without getting wet has crumbled away.  The western wall, unlike the
others, is made of huge grey stone that remind you of the town walls.
Water gushes in from the south and east and runs off to the north.

rooms.name: In a Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are standing in a sewer tunnel perched on a thin ledge on one wall.
Below you, water full of filth and dirt rushes by from east to west.  The
brick walls here are old, seemingly older than the rest of the sewer sys-
tem.  You can go east or west.

rooms.name: In a Sewer Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are standing on a little ledge on one brick wall of this sewer pipe.
Just below you, somewhat clean water runs from the east to west.  Through
pipes in the ceiling, great flows of filth plop down into the water here
to be embrased and swept away.  You can go west or east.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
Here, a large pipe running east-west is joined by a strange tunnel leading
north.  The tunnel to the north seems to be older than these sewers and its
floor is dry -- protected from water by a tall legde.  Water here runs from
east to west and appears to be somewhat clean still.  You may go north, east,
or west.

rooms.name: At a Junction in the Sewers
rooms.desc:
This is a large subterranean chamber far underneath the city of Alaozar.
Here, water rushes in through a big pipe to the north and flows away
through a tunnel leading west.  There is a raised tunnel leading away
to the east and since the water level is low it is still dry.  You may
go north, west, or east.

rooms.name: In the Overflow Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This tunnel was surely designed to fill only if the water level of the
Chartuse River rose dangerously high to prevent damage to the sewer
system and flooding in the streets above.  The ground here is not bone
dry but rather moldy and slightly moist.  You suspect this place gets
its share of water every now and then when the rains are heavy.  You
can go west or south from this point.

rooms.name: In a Dry Tunnel
rooms.desc:
The walls here are made of the same re-inforced grey stone that was used
in the city walls and if your sense of direction is right you must be
either next to or underneath those massive walls right now.  This passage
leads off to the north and south.

rooms.name: In the Overflow Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are in some kind of overflow tunnel; the amount of water here is minimal
and it is raised several feet above the other sewer tunnels you have seen.
Clearly this tunnel was built to prevent flooding or damage that might be
caused in the event of a water level rise.  You can go north or east from
here.

rooms.name: In the Overflow Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You are standing in a tunnel designed to act as an overflow tunnel so
that if the water level in the sewers rose too high it would fill and
help alleviate the pressure and reduce the risk of flooding.  Right now,
there is very little water here and you can see the thick mold and slime
on the brick tunnel floor.  There is a huge brick pit here leading down
into the darkness.  Perhaps the engineers thought that this "well" would
take even more overflowing waters back to the earth or some underground
river?  You could probibly climb down.  The overflow tunnel here leads
both east and west.

rooms.name: In the Overflow Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This tunnel was built as a way to prevent flooding in the rainy season
when the Chartuse River's level typically rises.  Right now there is
very little water on the ground here and you walk over strange green
mold which, like a carpet, covers the floor.  You can go east or west.

rooms.name: In the Overflow Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This is a mostly dry tunnel with a very large diameter and a lot of
mold growing on the walls and floor.  It leads both west and east.

rooms.name: In the Overflow Tunnel
rooms.desc:
This tunnel changes direction here, sloping gradually downward to the west
while rising slightly to the north.  Since this entire area is a few feet
higher than the rest of the sewer network, you assume it was built to help
reduce pressure on the other tunnels when the water level rose in rainy
times.  You can go north or west.

rooms.name: In a Secret Passageway
rooms.desc:
This passage is clearly not part of the sewers.  Instead it was built
of the same stone used to make the city walls.  There are a few old
chairs here and what look like cases to store weapons.  Could this
way have once been guarded by soldiers from the city?  You can go
north or east.

rooms.name: Under the Walls!
rooms.desc:
This must be a secret passageway under the city walls!  The stones all
around you look just like the massive grey ones used to build the huge
walls protecting Alaozar.  You are far below the ground and suspect you
have found a secret tunnel out of the city.  Perhaps it was made so that
if ever beseiged, soldiers from Alaozar could smuggle in food or get out
to sneak attack the enemy.  You can go east or west.

rooms.name: In a Small Tunnel!
rooms.desc:
This tunnel is very small and difficult to move through.  It leads both
east and west into the darkness.

rooms.name: In a Small Tunnel!
rooms.desc:
This tunnel is very small and difficult to move through.  It leads both
east and west into the darkness.

rooms.name: In an underground river!
rooms.desc:
The current is not as strong here and you have a moment to rest and
breathe again.  While you can not find the strength to move back against
the water to the north, there is a little crack in the southern wall that
you just might be able to fit through...

rooms.name: In an underground river!
rooms.desc:
SPUTTER... you are being swept along by an underground river.  It is very
difficult to breathe here and there are huge rocks above your head that
you are trying to avoid being swept into.  The water here is freezing
cold and you are beginning to lose feeling in your limbs.  At some places
it is all you can do to find air pockets to breathe in!  Although this
stream seems to run north and south, the current here is way too strong
to fight by moving north.  You can only swim south, with the current.

rooms.name: In an underground river!
rooms.desc:
COUGH... you just swallowed some of this mineral-rich water and almost
choked when it went down the wrong passage.  You are struggling with
this very swift underground river and are being swept along to the
south by the current.  You can hardly breathe... ...and if that were
not enough you are worried about the low-hangling stalagtites and that
this damn river threatons to bach you into.  The water rushes north to
south and is impossible to move against.

rooms.name: In an underground river!
rooms.desc:
WHEW... you just missed a huge, low-hanging rock that, at the speed this
water is carrying you, would have dashed the life out of you.  The river
is very cold and you are beginning to lose feeling in your arms and legs.
To top it all off, you can hardly breathe!  The current is too strong to
fight by moving north and the only direction you can move is south, with
the flow.

rooms.name: In an underground river!
rooms.desc:
GASP... you are being swept along by an underground river.  It is very
difficult to breathe here and there are huge rocks above your head that
you are trying to avoid being swept into.  The current is carrying you
in a southward direction and it is impossible to fight.  The best move
might be just to take a deep breath, dive under, and hope for the best!

rooms.name: In an underground river!
rooms.desc:
SPLASH... you fall right into a raging subterranean stream and are
immediately caught in the strong current.  The rapids pull you
under and it is all you can do to breathe.  The mineral-rich water
is frigid and your limbs start to lose feeling.  You cannot reach the
wall to hang on and are being inexoirable swept southward!
